Shelf has one relevant fact, from docs.saltmarsh.example/limits read 2026-08-21:

  - hosted runners: a job is cancelled after 6 hours
  - a whole pipeline run: 72 hours
  - jobs queued more than 24 hours are dropped
  - self-hosted runners: no job time limit

So your ~7 hour nightly job would be killed at the 6-hour mark on a hosted runner, before it finishes. Two ways out: run it on a self-hosted runner (no job cap), or split it into stages that each stay under 6 hours — the 72-hour pipeline limit and the 24-hour queue limit are not the binding constraint here.

Two caveats: the fact is a 6-hour job ceiling on hosted runners, and this reading is about two months old (2026-08-21), so check the limits page again before you build around it. The other match in the shelf (Corvane multipart limits) is unrelated.
